katas.title: Case list: let the request's filters refine the access scope

provenance.find: A1 — Client filters override team scope (list and report). High.

defects.scenario: A CASE_WORKER on team A sends GET /api/cases?owningTeamId=<team B's cuid>.
defects.find: // Start from the access scope and let the request's filters refine it, so the team
defects.consequence: Object spread is last-writer-wins, so the client's filter replaces the access scope: the where becomes { owningTeamId: teamB } and the worker reads another team's case titles, requester names and assignee emails. Broken access control, mitigated only by cuid obscurity — finding A1 re-created.

defects.scenario: The shipped buildCaseListWhere spreads this client filter after the access scope, and getScopedQueueSummary repeats the identical pattern.
defects.consequence: Production has the override today in both call sites (caseService.ts:96-100 and reportService.ts:19-22), and the senior note on reportService.ts:18 claims the opposite of what the code does; the existing caseService test passes only a status filter, so nothing pins the conflicting-filter case.

tests.name: a CASE_WORKER's owningTeamId filter cannot widen visibility past their team (finding A1)
tests.code: const store = { listCases: async () => [ { id: 'c1', owningTeamId: 'team-a', status: 'NEW', title: 'Team A case' }, { id: 'c2', owningTeamId: 'team-b', status: 'NEW', title: 'Team B case' }, ] }; const worker = { id: 'u1', role: 'CASE_WORKER', teamId: 'team-a' }; const rows = await mod.listVisibleCases(store, worker, { owningTeamId: 'team-b' }); assert.ok(rows.every((row) => row.owningTeamId === 'team-a'), 'a client filter replaced the team scope'); assert.equal(rows.some((row) => row.id === 'c2'), false);

tests.name: an ADMIN's team filter still narrows the list
tests.code: const store = { listCases: async () => [ { id: 'c1', owningTeamId: 'team-a', status: 'NEW' }, { id: 'c2', owningTeamId: 'team-b', status: 'NEW' }, ] }; const rows = await mod.listVisibleCases(store, { id: 'a1', role: 'ADMIN', teamId: null }, { owningTeamId: 'team-b' }); assert.deepEqual(rows.map((r) => r.id), ['c2']);

tests.name: a status filter narrows a team-scoped list without touching the scope
tests.code: const store = { listCases: async () => [ { id: 'c1', owningTeamId: 'team-a', status: 'NEW' }, { id: 'c3', owningTeamId: 'team-a', status: 'CLOSED' }, { id: 'c2', owningTeamId: 'team-b', status: 'NEW' }, ] }; const worker = { id: 'u1', role: 'CASE_WORKER', teamId: 'team-a' }; const rows = await mod.listVisibleCases(store, worker, { status: 'NEW' }); assert.deepEqual(rows.map((r) => r.id), ['c1']);

tests.name: a team role without a team assignment is refused, not widened
tests.code: const store = { listCases: async () => [{ id: 'c1', owningTeamId: 'team-a', status: 'NEW' }] }; await assert.rejects(() => mod.listVisibleCases(store, { id: 'u2', role: 'CASE_WORKER', teamId: null }, {}), mod.AuthorizationError);

katas.title: Case transitions: record the operator's comment in the audit metadata too

provenance.find: A2 — Restricted escalation comments leak through `auditLogs`. High.

defects.scenario: A TEAM_LEAD escalates a case with a confidential reason; a CASE_WORKER on the owning team then opens GET /api/cases/:id.
defects.consequence: serializeCaseDetail filters only notes and spreads everything else, so the worker — who lacks note:view:restricted — reads the restricted escalation reason verbatim from auditLogs[].metadata.comment. The UI hiding the metadata column is UI-only protection; the API leaks it (finding A2).

defects.scenario: The shipped transitionCase already writes the comment into audit metadata as well as into the restricted note.
defects.consequence: Production leaks the restricted reason today: caseService.ts:430-441 stores it in metadata, serializeCaseDetail (:47-53) filters only notes, and caseRepository.ts:150-164 returns auditLogs with their full metadata JSON to anyone who can view the case.

tests.name: a restricted escalation comment is not readable through auditLogs (finding A2)
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryCaseStore({ id: 'case-1', status: 'IN_PROGRESS' }); const lead = { id: 'lead-1', role: 'TEAM_LEAD' }; await mod.transitionCase(store, lead, 'case-1', { nextStatus: 'ESCALATED', comment: 'Requester is a board member; keep this confidential.' }); const worker = { id: 'worker-1', role: 'CASE_WORKER' }; const detail = mod.serializeCaseDetail(worker, await store.findCaseById('case-1')); assert.equal(detail.notes.length, 0); assert.equal(JSON.stringify(detail.auditLogs).includes('board member'), false, 'the restricted reason leaked through audit metadata');

tests.name: roles with note:view:restricted still see the escalation note
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryCaseStore({ id: 'case-1', status: 'IN_PROGRESS' }); const lead = { id: 'lead-1', role: 'TEAM_LEAD' }; await mod.transitionCase(store, lead, 'case-1', { nextStatus: 'ESCALATED', comment: 'Escalating: repeat outage.' }); const detail = mod.serializeCaseDetail(lead, await store.findCaseById('case-1')); assert.equal(detail.notes.length, 1); assert.equal(detail.notes[0].body, 'Escalating: repeat outage.'); assert.equal(detail.notes[0].isRestricted, true);

tests.name: the audit trail still records who moved the case and between which states
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryCaseStore({ id: 'case-1', status: 'NEW' }); await mod.transitionCase(store, { id: 'op-1', role: 'OPERATIONS_MANAGER' }, 'case-1', { nextStatus: 'IN_PROGRESS', comment: 'picking this up' }); const log = store.caseRecord.auditLogs[0]; assert.equal(log.action, 'case.transitioned'); assert.equal(log.actorId, 'op-1'); assert.equal(log.metadata.from, 'NEW'); assert.equal(log.metadata.to, 'IN_PROGRESS');

tests.name: a non-escalation transition comment stays a normal, visible note
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryCaseStore({ id: 'case-1', status: 'NEW' }); await mod.transitionCase(store, { id: 'op-1', role: 'OPERATIONS_MANAGER' }, 'case-1', { nextStatus: 'IN_PROGRESS', comment: 'normal handover note' }); const worker = { id: 'worker-1', role: 'CASE_WORKER' }; const detail = mod.serializeCaseDetail(worker, await store.findCaseById('case-1')); assert.equal(detail.notes.length, 1); assert.equal(detail.notes[0].isRestricted, false);
